summary: Adds two publishing pipelines for the imported @cipherstash/auth napi packages (release.yml auth-artifacts/publish-auth via a new reusable _build-auth-artifacts.yml, plus a manual auth-preflight.yml) and for the stack-auth/stack-profile crates (release-plz.yml release-crates with a new root release-plz.toml). Both are inert at head: the npm jobs only run when the gate reports auth=true, and while the seven auth packages are in FROZEN_PUBLISHERS that state makes the gate exit non-zero first; the crates job is keyed on the same @cipherstash/auth entry. The live behaviour changes today are small: the release gate now classifies auth names separately (auth instead of js), the Release job waits on publish-auth, and release-plz.yml triggers on more paths, which also runs the armed EQL crate job more often. The material risk is latent and lands at the arming PR: the auth musl leg is built without the -crt-static flag the protect-ffi pipeline uses, and neither the release path nor the preflight would catch a statically linked musl binary, so a broken binary could be published irreversibly. Also, once armed, a failure in any of the six auth builds holds every JS release. Static workflow tests were added but not run here (no node_modules, no CI results).

behaviour_changes.description: release-gate.mjs classify() returns a third flag `auth` for names starting with @cipherstash/auth; those names no longer count toward `js`. The gate writes ffi/auth/js to GITHUB_OUTPUT and the gate job exposes `auth` as an output.

release.yml gains auth-artifacts (calls the new reusable build of six napi binaries + wasm + wrapper) and publish-auth (npm OIDC publish of six platform tarballs then the wrapper, git tags, GitHub release). Both run only in production mode when gate.outputs.auth == 'true'.
The Release job (changeset publish, Version Packages PR, and the EQL production chain hanging off it) now needs publish-auth and requires it to have succeeded whenever gate.outputs.auth == 'true'.

release-plz.yml adds crates-armed + release-crates (publish-only release-plz run against the root workspace with release-plz.toml), armed when @cipherstash/auth leaves FROZEN_PUBLISHERS. Its push path filter now also includes packages/stack-auth/**, packages/stack-profile/**, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, release-plz.toml and cliff.toml, which starts the whole workflow, including the already-armed EQL `release` job, on those pushes.

The seven @cipherstash/auth packages become a changesets `fixed` group, and each gains a `repository` field (needed for npm provenance). A new manual workflow, auth-preflight.yml, builds the tarballs, checks architecture and libc statically, and smoke-loads the linux-x64-gnu pair.

Static tests are added or extended for the gate classification, the arming switch for the crates line, the release-plz.toml membership, the build workflow shape and the repository URLs. The lint target lists and the supply-chain path filters now include the two new workflows.

failure_scenarios.title: linux-x64-musl auth binary built statically (no -crt-static) and published without any check that would notice
failure_scenarios.trigger: The arming PR removes the @cipherstash/auth entries and a version bump makes gate report auth=true, so auth-artifacts builds and publish-auth publishes.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The musl leg of _build-auth-artifacts.yml installs only musl-tools and runs `napi build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` (lines 68-73, 116). It sets no RUSTFLAGS, and the auth crate's .cargo/config.toml sets flags only for macOS. The protect-ffi pipeline explicitly exports `-C target-feature=-crt-static` for the same target (_build-ffi-artifacts.yml:238) so that the binary links musl dynamically. With Rust's crt-static default on musl, the auth cdylib is either dropped (a loud build failure) or produced self-contained. The release path checks only that a non-empty .node file exists and is in the tarball (lines 131, 163). The manual preflight's musl check only asserts there is NO glibc NEEDED entry (auth-preflight.yml:91-95), which a static binary also satisfies, and the smoke test loads only linux-x64-gnu (line 109).
failure_scenarios.consequence: @cipherstash/auth-linux-x64-musl could ship a .node that fails to load, or crashes, on Alpine/musl hosts. Every stack/CLI install on those hosts would hit 'Failed to load native binding'. npm publishes cannot be undone, so recovery needs a new version of all seven packages.

failure_scenarios.title: Once armed, any auth build failure holds every JS and EQL npm release
failure_scenarios.trigger: After arming, a release that bumps the auth group hits a failure in any of the six platform builds or in the wasm/wrapper job (e.g. runner image change, the gate's frozen-bytes or tree-drift checks, wasm-pack/mise download failure).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: publish-auth is skipped when auth-artifacts fails. The Release job requires `needs.gate.outputs.auth != 'true' || needs.publish-auth.result == 'success'` (release.yml:478-482), so changeset publish, the Version Packages PR update and the EQL production chain (eql-sql/eql-docs/eql-image need `release`) all skip. Because changesets uses `fixed` groups, an auth bump can travel in the same Version PR as unrelated packages.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Releases of @cipherstash/stack, stash and @cipherstash/eql are delayed until the auth build is fixed or the auth bump is split out. The design fails closed, so nothing broken ships.

failure_scenarios.title: Widened release-plz.yml triggers start the armed EQL crate job on unrelated root-workspace pushes
failure_scenarios.trigger: A push to main that touches only Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, release-plz.toml, cliff.toml or the stack-auth/stack-profile crates.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The new paths sit in the workflow-level `on.push.paths` (release-plz.yml:47-54), so eql-armed and the EQL `release` job (line 86) run as well as crates-armed. The EQL job queries crates.io, and if the eql-bindings version is not on crates.io it enforces the SQL-stamp guard, imports the GPG key and runs release-plz release for packages/eql. The non-cancelling `release-plz` concurrency group serialises the runs.
failure_scenarios.consequence: There are more EQL release runs, each normally a no-op. If an eql-bindings version is left unpublished, it publishes on whichever push comes next, or a crates.io API failure turns an unrelated push red. The failure is visible and recoverable.

evidence.claim: AUTH_PREFIX and classify() now return {ffi, auth, js}; auth names are excluded from js.
The gate writes ffi/auth/js outputs before checking blockers, then exits 1 on any blocker (including an unpublished frozen package), which fails the gate job.
auth-artifacts and publish-auth run only when mode == production and gate.outputs.auth == 'true', with no always(), so a failed gate skips them.
publish-auth publishes the six platform tarballs, then the wrapper, with npm OIDC provenance, skipping versions already on npm.
The Release job needs publish-auth and requires its success whenever gate.outputs.auth == 'true'.
crates-armed runs `node scripts/eql-pipeline-armed.mjs crates`; release-crates runs release-plz release on the root workspace only when armed.
Workflow-level push paths now include the root Cargo files, release-plz.toml, cliff.toml and the two crates, alongside packages/eql/**; the EQL `release` job has no further path gating.
The seven auth packages are added as a changesets fixed group; they are workspace members via pnpm-workspace.yaml's auth/platforms/* glob.
auth-preflight is workflow_dispatch-only, with contents: read.
The tests cover the crates line keying on @cipherstash/auth, independence from the EQL entry, and that only release-crates is gated on crates-armed. Not run.
The tests cover classify() for auth names, the three GITHUB_OUTPUT flags, and the Release job's wait on publish-auth. Not run.
The musl leg installs musl-tools and runs napi build with --target only, with no RUSTFLAGS. The post-build checks are only that the .node exists, is non-empty and is in the tarball.
The catalog `repo` pins @cipherstash/auth and its six platform packages at 0.44.0 for consuming packages.
The protect-ffi musl build exports RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=-crt-static' to keep the binary dynamically linked against musl.
The musl check only asserts the absence of a glibc NEEDED entry. The smoke install uses the linux-x64-gnu tarball only.
The auth crate's cargo config sets rustflags only for macOS targets.
eql-sql (and eql-docs/eql-image after it) need the Release job, so a skipped Release skips the EQL production artefacts.
